  "text": "The man on the stairs wore his father's coat. It had been too large for his father and was too small for him. His wrists showed beneath the cuffs.

“Those won't cover it,” he said.

The boy put a penny on its edge. It fell against another with a small, ordinary sound.

“How much?”

The woman closed her fingers around the stone.

“Don't ask prices in this house.”

The man came down one step. There was mud on his socks, no shoes. He looked at the cupboard with an expression the boy remembered from mirrors: annoyance, quickly arranged to resemble concern.

“She'll say anything to stay.”

Inside the cupboard, Anne moved her foot. The door opened another inch.

“Get my slipper,” she said.

He reached through the gap. Her ankle was warm. That was worse than if it had been cold, and he nearly let go.

“Just the slipper.”

He eased it off. Something hard lay beneath the flattened lining, pressing up through a split in the cloth.

The man descended another step.

“I put that there for safekeeping.”

The boy worked a fingernail into the split and drew out a little brass key.

Behind him, the woman set her stone on the floor. Very carefully, she rested one shoe upon it.

“Now,” she said, “we can discuss which of you lives here.”

The man stopped smiling.

The boy hadn't noticed that he'd been smiling until he stopped.

“What does it open?” he asked.

Anne's bare toes curled against the threshold.

“Nothing,” she said. “It locks the front door.”

From the stairs, the man said, “You wouldn't leave me outside.”"
